translation:
In devotion to Vishnu, the merchant-thief is encountered; within this comes the question of Ekadashi: 1. Omkar, 2. The extent of the glory of the Name — the words of Kabirji and Nabhaji. The second question, on Ekadashi, follows — so said the Vaishnav. Let us look now at what Kabirji has said about the merchant-thief.

_Kahenku shaha aur vritti hai chorki, shahaji kehet nahi sharam aavai.
Jooth hi kehet aur jooth hi rahet hai, ren din joothme janam jaavai.
Manne kai aasre aur phool kari vaithiya, indriyan swad man mahi bhaavai.
Kehet Kabir te sahaku boliye, jamrayeke dhesle khoob khaavai._
(One who is called a merchant-banker but whose true disposition is that of a thief — such a "shah" feels no shame at all in speaking falsehood. He speaks only lies and lives only by lies; his days and nights pass away lost in falsehood. Relying on people's trust in him, he swells with vanity, and his mind delights in the pleasures of the senses. Kabir says: such a one, though called a "sahukar" (honest merchant), shall receive many blows from the club of Yama's messengers.)

Servant Kabirji says: there are those who have themselves called "sajjan" (gentleman) and "mahajan" (respected merchant) merely for the name of it, while their true disposition is one of dishonesty. One feels ashamed even to call such people "mahajan" or "sajjan." They speak only falsehood, and their conduct too is bad; their whole life, day and night, passes in doing wrong. Sheltering behind the good name of "shahukar" and "mahajan," they carry on their household customs while continuing the very same wrongdoing, and all the while the pleasures of the senses remain very dear to their minds. Servant Kabirji says: such a false "shahukar" has been told plainly that he shall receive many blows from the club of Yamraj.

_Swangse Har tajiye nahi, jaane vastu apaar.
Baharvasi Govinddas, koi ditho shahukar. ||11||_
(One should not abandon Hari for the sake of an outward disguise, knowing the true substance to be beyond measure. Govinddas, who dwells only in outward show, asks: has anyone, anywhere, ever truly seen a genuine shahukar?)

Govinddas, a disciple of Sadguru Jivandasji Maharaj (who had given up being a brahmin to become a devotee of Uda), says: among those who follow a false, deceptive outward show — full of countless kinds of cunning trickery — and who, in following it, remain averse to devotion to God, no truly worthy gentleman or genuine devotee is ever to be found.

_Mata to Sita khari, aur mata manho mai.
Aadha le bolayke, piche mele khai. ||53||_
(Only Sita is the true Mother; every other so-called mother is but a deceiver. She calls one halfway to her with sweet words, and afterward throws him into the pit.)

Jivandasji Maharaj says: for us, the only Mother truly worthy of worship is Mother Sita. Any other mother — the goddess Shakti, who casts beings into the eighty-four lakh species of the cycle of birth — is of no use to me. For that goddess separates us from Hari, the Guru, and the saints; she lures us into base forms of worship, turns us away from devotion to God, and then makes us her prey.

Gods and goddesses and the like hold out temptations to us. On this subject it is written, in Register No. 887, page 52: those who perform yajnas and other rites out of worldly desire are regarded by the gods as their own cattle. This is because, should such people attain knowledge through devotion and become true devotees of God, their sense of separateness from the Supreme would dissolve, and they would be freed from ritual action. And once freed from ritual action, the gods would lose their share of offerings from such yajnas. For this reason, the gods place many kinds of obstacles before one who sets out to attain knowledge and devotion; at such times one must remain unshaken.

The occasion of the question about Ekadashi: the Vaishnav Jivandasji spoke — once, at a certain time, when Shri Vasudevji lay resting, there is this Vedantic verse describing it:

_Kararavindena padaravindam mukharavinde vinivesha yam te.
Vatasya patrasya pute shayanam balam Mukundam manasa smarami._
(I meditate in my mind upon the infant Lord Mukunda, who holds His lotus-foot to His lotus-mouth with His lotus-hand, and who lies resting upon the surface of a banyan leaf.)

This episode occurs in the Matsya Purana, chapter 166. Markandeyaji saw a beautiful child sleeping upon the banyan tree, sucking the thumb of his own foot. Of this the poet writes:

_Vihaya piyusha rasam munishwara mamanghri rajiva rasam pivanti kim.
Iti swa padambuja pana kautuki sa gopa balah shriyam aatanotu vah._
(Setting aside the nectar of immortality as trifling, do the great sages instead drink the essence of My lotus feet — why should this be? Is it perhaps more delicious even than nectar? Wondering thus, and playfully drinking the nectar of His own lotus foot, may that cowherd-child bestow prosperity upon you.)

In childhood, an infant puts the toe of his own foot into his mouth and sucks it. Do not think that Krishna, in his form as the cowherd-child, was free of this habit either — he too had it, but not, as with ordinary infants, without reason; his had a purpose. He wondered: why do great sages and seers, setting aside even the nectar of immortality as trifling, drink instead the essence of My lotus feet — is it perhaps more delicious even than nectar? It was to test this very question that the infant Krishna used to play this game of drinking from His own foot. May that same glorious child increase the well-being of Kalyan and his guardians.

The child-form upon the leaf of the banyan tree — Bhagavatam, Canto 12, Chapter 9, verse 21:

_Praguttarasyam shakhayam tasyapi dadrshe shishum.
Shayanam parni-putake grasantam prabhaya tamah. ||21||_
(On a branch of that tree facing the northeast, he saw a child lying within the fold of a leaf, dispelling the darkness by his own radiance.)

Wandering through the ocean of dissolution, one day Markandeya Muni's gaze fell upon a small banyan tree standing on a high stretch of ground, adorned with fruit and fresh green leaves. Within the fold of a leaf on a branch in the northeast corner of that tree, he saw a child lying, shining and radiant, dispelling the darkness by his own splendour. Seeing this wondrous sight, he went up to the child in fear, meaning to question him; but even as he approached, along with the child's breath, Markandeya Muni, like a mosquito, was drawn inside the child's body.

At the time of dissolution, when the world lay submerged in water, Lord Narayan lay resting with the pillow of yogic sleep. From His navel, Brahma was born upon a lotus leaf. Brahma looked all around and saw only water everywhere. Brahma then performed austerities for eighty-four thousand years, during which sixty yugas passed in the mortal world. He then descended into the lotus leaf, and there Lord Brahma uttered "Om." Having bowed in reverence, Brahma took up this mantra — this is how the Omkar mantra received its name, and its glory was magnified. Why, for what reason, and in what way it was magnified is explained as follows.

Brahmaji descended into the stalk of the lotus and there uttered the syllable "Om." Then the gracious Lord replied, "Soham" — meaning: if you say "Oham" [I am He], then that too is I Myself; you too have manifested from Me. Seekers have taken up these words, "Oham" and "Soham," as a means of worship, but Kabir did not consider them fitting for devotion to God. To clarify this, the revered Yadunath, in the Chhuti Kapli discourse of the Samagam, has recorded the following couplets of Kabir:

_Omkar nishchai bhaya, so karta mati jaan.
Sancha shabda Kabirka, parde mahi pichhan. ||20||_
(Understand for certain what Omkar truly is — do not take it to be the Creator himself. The true word of Kabir is this: recognize the reality that lies hidden behind the veil.)

Servant Kabirji says: regarding Omkar, this is the conclusion reached — do not take it to be the Creator of the universe. Rather, it is the Supreme Being, Parabrahma Paramatma — who deceives both the wise and the simple alike, remaining ever apart, performing His great play; day and night, O Adhyaru, may Hari Parabrahm be victorious — who is the one that manifests Omkar and who also dissolves it, and who secretly governs and runs all creation. The utterance of Ram-nam that Kabir has taught is the true and genuine word of the Name of God.

_Jo jan houhai jai Hari, ratan lehi bilagay.
Sohang sohang jari miya, mithya janam gamay. ||21||_
(Whoever is truly a devotee of Hari will set the jewel apart from the false. But he who merely burns his life away chanting "Soham, Soham" wastes his birth in falsehood.)

Servant Kabirji says: whoever are discerning, wise, saintly persons will set the jewel of Ram's Name apart from the false, illusory, stone-like practice of mere chanting; but people without discernment, foolishly chanting "Oham, Soham, Soham" and the like, waste their birth in illusory Maya.

_Kabir pargat Ram kahu, chhanai Ram na gaay.
Phoosak joda doori karu, bahuri na laage laay. ||30||_
(Kabir says: proclaim Ram's Name openly; do not sing of Ram in secret. Cast off the false, straw-like covering, and the fire of worldly desire will never touch you again.)

Servant Kabirji says: O devotees! Worship the manifest, self-luminous form of Ram; do not keep Him hidden. Do not worship Ram in secret and stealth, the way a mantra is whispered into the ear. Cast off the straw-and-grass garment — the ego of the body born of Maya — and then the fire of the threefold afflictions arising from sense-pleasures will never touch you again.

For the seeker, it is best to stay well away from "Soham." The meaning of "Soham" is "I am Brahman." This tree, beneath which you and I now sit, is a creation of Brahman. Let the one who says "Soham" make just such a tree and show it to us — then it could be understood that he has truly reached the rank of Brahman; otherwise it is nothing but empty raving.

_E roop aroope shamalo, khele Nand dwar.
Aadi Omkar upanyo, koti brahmand vistar._
(This dark-hued Lord, who is both formed and formless, plays at Nand's doorway. In the beginning Omkar arose from Him, and from it spread crores of universes.)

Jivandasji Maharaj says: this Lord Krishna, who is in truth formless, takes on form and plays in the courtyard of Nandji. From the navel of that same Krishna, Omkar first arose in the beginning, and from it spread forth crores of universes.

_Mansa Devi upani, taathe bhayo ahankar.
Ghat-ghat vyapak jeevana, so khele Nand dwar._
(From Him arose the goddess Mansa, and from her arose the ego. That same Lord, pervading every single body, plays at Nand's doorway.)

Jivandasji Maharaj says: at the beginning of creation, a goddess named Mansa (a goddess of illusion) arose, and from her the Omkar-based, three-natured creation came into being. The essence of that same Parabrahma Paramatma pervades every single body in the world; and that same Supreme Being plays in the courtyard of Nandji.

The Name of Ram (Register No. 1, pages 142–143; Jagdish, Register No. 179, pages 46–47).

One should hold firm faith in God. Those who possess complete faith in the Supreme Being, together with knowledge of His glory, succeed in all their undertakings; not only that, they are able to accomplish even tasks that appear impossible to others. But those whose minds lack such firm faith, together with knowledge of His glory, cannot bring even their own difficult undertakings to success, let alone those of others. The following story likewise conveys this same point.

A great soul (Kabirji) was once sitting on the bank of a river, singing devotional songs to Govind. At that time a hunter came out of the forest. Just then no boat was to be had, and he grew anxious, for it was urgent that he cross to the other side without delay, and owing to certain difficulties a boat could not quickly be found. Seeing him in this troubled state, Shri Kabirji, who happened to be sitting there, asked him in his own easy manner the reason for his worry. The hunter said, "What work do you do?" The master replied, "I worship Vasudev." The hunter then asked, "What is gained by worshipping Him?" The great soul replied, "One crosses the ocean of worldly existence." The hunter said, "But this river has so much water in it — can one cross that too?" The great soul replied, "If one can cross crores upon crores of oceans, what is this river beside that?" The hunter then began to press him: "Give me some remembrance of the Name — I must reach my dwelling." The great soul said, "Close your eyes," and, taking the hunter's right hand, wrote upon it the divine Name, "Ram," and said, "Now you shall be able to walk over the water in comfort to your dwelling place; by the power of this Name you will not drown." The hunter then began walking on the water as though on solid ground. Believing that he had been given a mighty and precious mantra, he went on his way with this understanding; and when he had very nearly reached the far shore, the thought arose in his mind: "Let me see, then, what kind of mantra I have been given." He looked, and saw the word "Ram" written there. Then it occurred to him: "Why, this is the very Ram-nam that I already know!" And as he said this, he began to sink and be swept away by the water.

At that moment a faint awareness of the mistake in his own words dawned on him, and he at once began to cry out that this was not his own Ram but Kabirji's Ram, who is supremely powerful. Through this, faith in the Name arose in him for that moment, and once again he began to walk as though through knee-deep water, and reached the far bank of the river in safety.

_Jap aru tap tirath vrat thothre, jog aru jaag sab dekhi chhoi.
Ek naam nikhyaan bin paar pahunche nahi, Bed aru Puraan padho koi.
Naam pratap tihu lok chhaana nahi, bhav sindhuke tiranku bana bhera.
Sant anek teer paar pele gaye, kahet Kabir nij naam tera._
(Repetition, austerity, pilgrimage, and vows are all worthless and without substance; I have examined yoga and yajna too. But without the one Name of God, no one has ever crossed the ocean of existence; let one read the Vedas and Puranas as much as one likes, still one does not cross over. The glory of the Name is not hidden in the three worlds; that Name was made to stay with us, to carry us across the ocean of existence. Many saints have already crossed to the far shore of that ocean — Kabir says, O Lord, this Name of Yours alone is supreme.)

Servant Kabirji says: japa, austerity, pilgrimage, and vows are all useless and without substance. I have examined both yoga and yajna, but in the end, without the one Name of God, none has ever crossed over worldly existence; even if one reads the Vedas and Puranas, still one does not cross over. The glory of God's Name is not hidden anywhere within the three worlds. That Name has been given to us so that it may stay with us and carry us across the ocean of existence. Many saints have crossed to the far side of that ocean — this Name of Yours is supreme indeed, so Kabirji says.

_Sapta koti maha-mantrash chitta vibhrama-karakah.
Eka eva paro mantro Rama ityakshara dvayam._
(There are seventy million great mantras, but all of them create confusion in the mind; above all of them, the two-syllabled mantra "Ram" alone is supreme.)

_Kabir pahunchenge tab kahenge, umadenge as thaam.
Ajahu bhela samudra men, bol bagcha kaay._
(Kabir will speak of arriving only once he has arrived; only then will he tell of overflowing in that Abode. For now he is still caught up amid the ocean — of what use, then, is idle boasting?)

Servant Kabirji says: once, with single-minded devotion, we have reached the final goal along the path shown by the Sadguru, only then shall we speak of our success — that having reached the Abode, we shall dwell there in joyous bliss. But for now we are still struggling within the atmosphere of the ocean of worldly existence; and so to boast in advance of how happy we shall be in that Abode is futile.

_Hoy viveki shabdake, jaay mile parivar.
Naam grahe pahunchahi, maano kaha hamar._
(Whoever is discerning about the Word shall attain the fellowship of devotees; whoever takes up the Name shall reach the goal — accept these, my words.)

The Sadguru, giving a word of caution, says: whichever devotees understand my teaching well and follow it shall attain the fellowship of devotees. Only those who take up the Name of God with single-minded devotion shall reach the Abode of the devotees — accept these, my words.

There, regarding Kabirji's initiation, are the words of Kabirji's biography (Parichay), in Vishram 1:

_Kautuk bhayo sakal sansara, Ramanandpe jaai pokara.
Musalman julaha ek, boojha naam tumhara lei.
(Kirtan kare bhagatanku sove.)
Tab Ramanande Kabir bolaya, aada padda beech devaya. ||12||
Hum kab diksha dini tohi, boojhat naam hamara lei.
Main raat raho gel men jaai, tab tum sevak seti nikse aai. ||13||
Tab tum moku Ram kahaya, main Ram kahat apne gher aaya.
Aise Ram kahat sab koi, in baat te tum bhagat na hoi. ||14||
Kabirka man niramal cheena, parda khol diksha deena.
Kabirke man bhayo aananda, bhaayeg mile guru Ramanand. ||19||_
(A great wonder arose in all the world; people ran crying out to Ramanand. "A Muslim weaver," they said, "questions us, taking your name." (He performs kirtan for devotees, and sleeps among them.) Then Ramanand summoned Kabir, and had a curtain set between them. "When did I ever give you initiation, that you should take my name?" "One night, as I lay in the road, you passed by with your servants" — "and your foot struck me, and you said 'Ram, Ram, wake up' — so I came home saying 'Ram Ram.'" "But everyone says 'Ram Ram' in that way — this alone does not make you my devotee." Then, perceiving that Kabir's mind was pure, Ramanand drew back the curtain and gave him initiation. Kabir's heart filled with joy at having found Guru Ramanand.)

A great wonder arose throughout the whole world — an astonishing thing had happened. People went crying out to Ramanand and said, "A Muslim weaver has taken up the vow of devotion to God! He practises devotion, has others practise it too, and serves the saints; and when asked by what right, he says you gave him initiation, and takes your name." Then Ramanand summoned Kabir and had a curtain placed between them, and said, "When did I ever give you initiation, that you should take my name?" Kabir replied, "One night, as I lay sleeping on the roadway, you happened to pass by with your attendants; your foot struck against me, and as you stumbled you said 'Ram, Ram' — so I woke up saying 'Ram Ram' and came home repeating it." Ramanand said, "In that case everyone naturally says 'Ram Ram' under such circumstances — this alone does not make you my disciple or devotee." But Kabirji, on one occasion, perceived that Ramanand, who was performing worship in his mind (mansi puja), had become stuck while placing a garland upon the Lord's ear, and said, "Why have you stopped there?" Since Kabir had thus known the very thought passing through Ramanand's mind, Ramanand recognized that Kabir's mind was pure, and drew back the curtain that had been placed between them, and gave him initiation. Kabirji was filled with joy that, by good fortune, he had obtained a Guru such as Ramanand.

_Akshar akshar ek jeevana, Omkarki aad.
Mamathe raro bado, Sadguru kahyo vichar. ||1||_
(Before every single syllable of every mantra, Omkar is placed. But greater still than this Omkar, the Sadguru — having reflected — has declared, is the letter "ra.")

Jivandasji Maharaj says: before each and every syllable of every kind of mantra, Omkar is placed. But greater than this form of Omkar is the letter "ra," which signifies the very essence of Ram's Name — so the Sadguru, having reflected and determined this, has said.

In the book Anabhe Vani, among the couplets of Ramcharandas, on page 49, in the section "Saar-grahika," couplet 2, it is said:

_Brahm shabda rakkar hai, maya roop makar.
Ramcharan yah jugal hai, nirakar aakar. ||2||_
(The syllable "ra" stands for the word Brahman; the syllable "ma" stands for the form of Maya. The word "Ram" is this very pair joined together — the formless and the formed.)

Ramcharandasji says: the letter "ra" occurring in the word "Ram" represents the Brahman-form of God, while the letter "ma" represents the form of Maya. Thus the word "Ram" is a word that joins together both Maya and Brahman: within it, the formless nature of God, which is the letter "ra," is joined with "ma," which represents God's Maya-linked, manifest form — thereby presenting the union of the formed and the formless.

The work accomplished by the one Name "Ram" is such that nothing else can equal it. From Shri Nabhaji's Bhaktamal:

_"Kabir" kripa te param tattva, "Padmanabh" parchau lahyau.
Naam mahanidhi mantra, naamhi seva pooja. Jap tap tirath naam, naam bin aur na dooja.
Naam preeti naam bair naam kahi naami baulai. Naam Ajamil sakhi, naam bandhan aur na dooja.
Naam adhik Raghunath te "Ram" nikat "Hanumat" kahyo.
'Kabir' kripa te param tattva, 'Padmanabh' parchau lahyau. ||68||_
(By Kabir's grace, Padmanabh attained the supreme reality. The Name is the great treasure-mantra; the Name alone is his service and worship. Repetition, austerity, pilgrimage — all are the Name; there is nothing else besides. Love through the Name, enmity through the Name, and it is the Name that speaks the Named One's own truth; Ajamil stands as witness to the Name — there is no other bond besides it. Hanuman declared to Raghunath's own face that the Name "Ram" is greater than Ram himself. By Kabir's grace, Padmanabh attained the supreme reality.)

By the grace of Shri Kabirdasji, Shri Padmanabhji came to know well the glory of the supreme reality, the Lord's Holy Name. The Holy Name of God alone was his supreme treasure; he regarded the Name alone as the great mantra. He performed his worship and service through the Name alone, considering the repetition of the Name itself to be the true worship of God, and regarding the repetition of the Name as encompassing every form of japa, austerity, and pilgrimage. He knew of no other means or goal besides the Holy Name. His worldly love and enmity, too, rested upon the Name alone — that is, he felt love for those devoted to the Name, and enmity toward those averse to the Name, its opponents; yet in both states he was, in truth, remembering the Name alone, holding firm faith that whether God's Name is uttered in love or in enmity, in either case Shri Nam Maharaj brings about one's ultimate good. He called the Name itself "Nami," that is, Parabrahma Paramatma. He held firm faith that the Holy Name of God alone frees the soul from the bondage of worldly existence. Shri Ajamilji is the witness to this supreme truth of Shri Nam Maharaj. Shri Ram-nam is greater even than Shri Ramji himself — this very thing Hanumanji declared to Ramji's own face.

Regarding this, Jivandasji said: it is by the power of that very Name that King Janak emptied the twenty-eight hells (naraka-kunds). It is by the strength of that Name that, in building the bridge across the ocean, Ram's Name was written upon the stones. By that same Name the hunter crossed over the water, yet was drowned by his own pride. Mahadevji holds fast to a single syllable — he takes refuge in "rankar," the letter "ra." Sheshji, with his thousand tongues, forever utters the Name of Ram; it is by the support of that Name alone that he bears the earth upon his hoods, and there Omkar is of no use at all.

_Rakarah sarva-devanam sakshat kaalanakah prabhuh. Rakarah sarva-jivana sarva-paapasya dahakah. ||1||
Rakarah sarva-bhootanam jeevaroop paraatparah. Rakarah sarva-devaanaam tej punja sanatanah. ||2||
Rakarah sarva-saukhyaanaam siddhidastu puraatanah. Rakarah sarva vidyaanaam vedyastattva sanatanah. ||3||
Rakarah sarva-bhootanam ishwaronanta roopadhruk. Rakarah sarva-jeevanaam vyaapya-vyaapakam ishwarah. ||4||
Rakaro utpadyate nityam rakaroleeyate jagat. Rakaro nirvikalpashcha shuddha sadaadvayah. ||5||
Rakarah sarva-kaamashcha paripoorna manoratha. Rakarah sarva-dushtaanaam naashako Raghunayakah. ||6||
Rakarah sarva-satvaanaam mahaamoda-maya swaraat. Rakarah sarva vedaanaam kaaranam prakriteparah. ||7||_
("Ra" is directly present in all the gods, like the great fire of dissolution; it is exceedingly radiant and supremely powerful, and it burns away all the sins of every soul. (1) "Ra" is the very life of all beings, the Supreme beyond the highest, and the very essence of radiance among all the gods. (2) "Ra" alone bestows all happiness and every accomplishment, and is primordial; "ra" alone is that which is known through every branch of knowledge. (3) "Ra" alone is the Lord who takes infinite forms in every being, and "ra" alone is the Lord who pervades and is pervaded in all living beings. (4) The whole creation is born from "ra" alone, is sustained by it, and again dissolves back into "ra"; and "ra" alone is the pure, blissful whole, the non-dual Brahman beyond all duality. (5) "Ra" alone fulfils every desire and wish; "ra" alone, in the form of Raghunayak (Ram), destroys all the wicked. (6) "Ra" alone is the giver of bliss to all beings, the Lord of lords; and "ra" alone carries one across the Vedas and is beyond Maya. (7))

At this very place, Shri Parvatiji, wishing to hear from Shri Shankarji of the power of Shri Ram's Name, asked the following question:

_Tatraiva Parvati vaavaryam Shri Shivam prati.
Gutika paatuka siddhih parakaay praveshham.
Vaachaa siddhish charth siddhistathaa siddhi manomayi. ||8||_
("O Lord! The power of the gutika-siddhi [invisibility], the paduka-siddhi [flight through sandals], the power to enter another's body, the power to enter water, the power to make one's word come true, and the power to accomplish whatever comes to mind — O beloved, knowing me as your handmaiden, tell me of these out of your grace.")

_Shri Shiva uvaacha - Sarveshvarya-prade sarva-siddhidam paramaartha-dam.
Mahaamaangalikam nityam Raamnaam paraatparam. ||1||
Naatah parataropaayo sukhaartha varttate priye. Satyam satyam punah satyam nanyathaa vachanam. ||12||_
(Shri Shivji replied: "O beloved, Shri Ram's Name, ever supremely auspicious, grants all lordship and all accomplishments, and bestows the ultimate good. O beloved, there is no other means for happiness greater than Shri Ram's Name; know this word of mine to be true, true, and true again — it is not otherwise.")

Shri Shivji replied that Shri Ram's Name, ever supremely auspicious, is the giver of all lordship and every accomplishment, and bestows the highest good; and that, for happiness, there is no other means beyond Shri Ram's Name — this word of his should be known as true, true, and true again.

Sushruti Samhita:

_Kaarakam pranavasyaapi Ramnaam jagadguruh.
Tasmaad dhyeyam sadaa chaitad yatibhih shuddha chetasaa._
(Shri Ram, the Guru of the universe, is himself the very cause of Omkar; therefore even renunciates should meditate upon the Name of Shri Ram with a pure mind.)

Pulastya Samhita:

_Rakaraat jaayate Brahma, rakaraat jaayate Harih.
Rakaraat jaayate Shambhu, rakaraat sarva shaktayah.
Beeje yathaa sthitih vrikshah shaakhaa pallava-sanyutah.
Tathaa vai sarva vedaahi rakaare suvyavasthitaah._
(From "ra" alone Brahma is born; from "ra" alone Vishnu is born; from "ra" alone Shankar is born; and from "ra" alone all powers arise. Just as a whole tree, with its branches and leaves, lies hidden within a tiny seed, so too, within the seed-syllable "ra," countless universes and all the Vedas lie secretly and fully arranged.)

Mahadevji holds fast to a single syllable — he takes refuge in "rankar," the letter "ra."

_Ramaini:_
_Sadguru Jeevan bal bal jau, guru parsade ramaini gaau.
Sadguru sanatan sunaya, mangal chaar rude dradhaya.
Tulsi tilak sant ki seva, ahar-nish dhyan Niranjan Deva.
Nirgun naam nirantar kahiya, sargun Raghupati leela lahiya.
Sargun kahiye kunj vihari, nirgun raas rame vanamaali.
Sakal sharir e Vraj vihari, aadya ramaini Radha pyaari.
Radha vasant Vrindavan maahi, adakshan leela alagi naahi.
Je ras leela Ved vakhaani, te ras leela gopi maani.
Je ras leela sant hi gaavai, Shuk Sanakaadik paar na paavai.
Raas ramaini vichaari gaavai, jeevanmukt param pad paavai._

I offer myself again and again to Sadguru Jivandasji; by his grace I sing this Ramaini. The Sadguru taught us the supreme Truth and established firm faith in the four essential things of the path of devotion: 1. Tulsi, 2. Tilak, 3. Company and service of the saints, and 4. Constant remembrance of the Name of God. The Name of God, belonging to the Parabrahma who is beyond the three gunas and without attributes (nirgun), is, he said, the eternal supreme Truth; and, through the play of His form with attributes (sagun), He is to be understood as Raghupati Ram. Further, His sagun form is that of Krishna, who plays in the groves; and that same Krishna, from beyond the gunas, plays the rasa dance. His entire form — both nirgun and sagun — is that of Krishna, who wanders and plays in Vraj; and His beloved companion, who has played with Him from the very beginning, is Radha. In Vrindavan the festival of spring goes on always; that divine play never ceases, even for a moment. The very sport whose glory the Vedas sing — the joy of that sport's essence is what the gopis know. The essence of that rasa-leela, which even the saints praise, is a mystery so deep that even Shukdev and the Sanaka brothers cannot fathom it. Whoever understands the true meaning of this Ramaini attains liberation-while-living and the supreme state.

Jivandasji Maharaj says: since this world was perishing in the dissolution, this three-natured essence of Omkar was of no use at all. But the essence of "rankar" remains unshaken, and the worshippers of "rankar" always remain forever established in the Supreme Abode.

Jivandasji Maharaj says: this creation has arisen from the three-natured Omkar; but those who have taken refuge in the Sadguru remain steadfast in the divine essence of "rankar."

_Rakar hai dash koti krishanu, kaana sahit sahasra dash bhanu.
Himkar koti hai makaara, ehi vidhi Raghupati naam udaara._
(The letter "ra" is as powerful as a hundred million fires; joined with the vowel "a" it becomes as radiant as ten thousand suns; and with "ma" added after it, it becomes as cooling as crores of ice — such, in this way, is the exceeding graciousness of Raghupati's Name.)

The letter "ra" is as powerful as a hundred million fires; joining the vowel-sign to it, it becomes as radiant as ten thousand suns; and adding "ma" after it, it becomes as cooling as crores upon crores of ice — such is the Name of Ram, exceedingly gracious.

_Teen naam hai Brahmake, aahang sohang Ram.
Ishtdevse bhajat hai, nyaare nyaare naam._
(There are three principal names of Brahman: Oham, Soham, and Ram; worshippers worship according to their own feeling for their chosen deity — God indeed has many different names.)

There are three principal names of the essence of Brahman-Paramatma: Oham, Soham, and Ram. Worshippers worship according to their own feeling for their chosen deity (ishtadev); God, indeed, has many different names.

_Soham gyaani rahat hai, yogi oyankaar.
Bhakt Ramko bhajat hai, kahai Kabir bichaar._
(Those on the path of knowledge dwell in "Soham"; yogis dwell in Omkar; and devotees worship Ram — so, having reflected, Kabir declares.)

Servant Kabirji, having reflected and decided, says: those on the path of knowledge worship through the word "Soham"; yogis worship through "Omkar"; and devotees worship Ram.

_Antar japiye Ramji, rom rom rankaar.
Rag ragar bole Ramji, sahajai hi dhun laagi rahai, yehi sumran saar._
(Within, repeat the Name of Ram, till "rankar" sounds in every hair of the body; let Ram's Name resonate in every vein, so that its melody flows on naturally — this is the essence of true remembrance.)

Servant Kabirji says: one should remember Ram's Name with such true sincerity of heart that the sound of Ram resonates in every vein, so that from every pore and hair of the body the sound of "rankar" arises. When the melody of Ram's Name thus flows naturally and spontaneously, that alone is called the true and proper remembrance of God's Name.

_Rankar anaadi Brahm hai, ehi Brahm videh.
Yaasu koi dooja kahai, taake muhade kheh._
(Rankar is the beginningless Brahman, the very Brahman beyond the body. Whoever claims there is another besides this, let dust fall into his mouth.)

Santdas says: "rankar" is the essence of Brahman from the very beginning, before all beginnings; that Parabrahma alone is the complete, Maya-transcending essence of God. If anyone claims that there is some other essence besides this, then let dust fall into his mouth — that is, let him be condemned.

_Rankar anaadi Brahm hai, Shiv bhi yehi kahant.
Arasi parasi hoi mili raha, koi koi virla sant._
(Rankar is the beginningless Brahman; Shiva too declares this. Only some rare, exceptional saint has attained its sight and touch and merged with it.)

Santdas says: "rankar" is the original name and form of Parabrahma; even Shivji recites, meditates upon, and remembers it. Only some rare, exceptional saint has ever, on some occasion, attained the vision and touch of that essence and merged with it.

_Kabir rankar akaarme, avigat gaya vilaay.
Avigatki tahaa gat nahi, to bhajai kaunku jaay._
(Kabir says: the formless nature of "rankar" dissolves into the formless Absolute; but that Absolute cannot itself be reached through it — so then, to what end should one worship it?)

Servant Kabirji says: the Omkar-nature contained within the essence of "rankar" dissolves and merges into Brahman-Parabrahma. Yet through this essence of Brahman alone, one cannot reach the essence of Parabrahma — so then why should anyone fall into the chains of such a lower Brahman and be forced to worship it?

_Kabir akshar bolte, Omkar anusaar.
Aakaarke bekaarko, moodh kahai Kirataar._
(Kabir says: people first utter the syllable "Om" before every mantra; this needless "Om," which serves no purpose, foolish people take to be the Creator himself.)

Servant Kabirji says: before every kind of mantra, people first utter a meaningless syllable such as "Om," and only then pronounce the mantra proper. This unnecessary "Om," which serves no real purpose at all, is taken by foolish people to be the Creator, God himself.

_Onhag sohang dehme, jap ajapa anoop.
Kahe Kabir so jaaniye, Sitapatiko roop._
(In the body, "Oham" and "Soham" arise — an incomparable repetition-without-repetition; Kabir says, know that this itself is the very form of Sitapati.)

Servant Kabirji says: when we breathe in, the sound "Oham" arises; and when we breathe out, the sound "Soham" arises. In this way, through the natural rhythm of the breath, the remembrance of God's Name, Ram-nam, goes on continuously and spontaneously, without the mouth ever uttering it and without any deliberate repetition at all. This is an exceedingly beautiful japa, one that goes on being repeated without any conscious repetition. Kabirji says: this spontaneous, effortless repetition is itself the very form of Sitapati Ram, the Lord of Sita.

_Oham so kaaya bhai, soham so man hoy.
Neh akshar su shwasa bhai, Dharmdas bhal joi._
(Oham becomes the body; Soham becomes the mind. This sound born of the breath is without letters — O Dharmdas, understand this well.)

Servant Kabirji says: the sense of "Oham" is our own body, and the sense of "Soham" is our own mind. Thus the sound of "Oham-Soham" is a sound without any of the fifty-two letters of the alphabet — O Dharmdas, understand this well.

_Shwasa so soham bhayo, soham so Omkar.
Oham soham so raro bhayo, Dharman karahu vichaar._
(From the breath arises Soham; from Soham arises Omkar; from Oham-Soham arises "ra" — O Dharmdas, reflect upon this.)

Servant Kabirji says: through the breath, the sound "Soham" arises, and from "Soham," "Oham" manifests; thus, after "Oham-Soham," the all-pervading sound of "rankar" comes forth. O Dharmdas, understand the mystery of this.

_Kabir Chand na hota, Soor na hota, nahi hota Oyankaar.
Tab Kabira Ramjan, kaha jaanai sansaar._
(Kabir says: when there was no moon, no sun, and no Omkar either, even then Kabir, servant of Ram, existed — how then could the world ever know him?)

Servant Kabirji says: when there was in creation neither moon, nor sun, nor even Omkar — before all that — there existed a manifestation of God whose very origin cannot be traced; how, then, could the people of this world ever come to know Him?

_Kabir dharti gagan pavan nahi, nahi tha wo Onkaar.
Tab Hari ke Harijan hote, kahe Kabir vichaar._
(Kabir says: when there was no earth, no sky, no wind, and no Omkar either, even then Hari and Hari's devotees already existed.)

Servant Kabirji says: when there was no earth, sky, air, water, or fire — none of the five great elements — and no Omkar either, even then Hari and Hari's devotees already existed. Kabirji, having reflected and reached this conclusion, declares it.

_Oyankaar pahelo Jeevana, sundar Shyam swaroop.
So Gokulme govaaliyo, je Dashrathkul badbhoop._
(Before Omkar itself, Jivan[dasji says], the beautiful dark-hued Lord existed; He dwells in Gokul as a cowherd, and He is the very one who reigned as a great king in the house of Dashrath.)

Jivandasji Maharaj says: before the very existence of Omkar, the beautiful, dark-hued Lord Shri Krishna already existed; He dwells in Gokul as a cowherd, and He is the very one who dwelt in the house of Dashrath as a great king.

_Naabhi kamal Brahma hua, so Gokulme govaal.
Aade Oankaar upno Jeevana, je kot Brahmaand vistaar._
(He from whose navel-lotus Brahma was born now dwells in Gokul as a cowherd; in the beginning, Jivan[dasji says], Omkar arose from Him, and from it spread crores of universes.)

Jivandasji Maharaj says: the same Brahma who was born from the lotus of the navel of the reclining Lord — that same Lord Shri Krishna now dwells in Gokul as a cowherd. At the time of the creation of this universe, it was Brahma who first uttered the syllable "Om"; and from that Om this three-natured universe spread forth.

_Oankaarke osare, bhoola sab sansaar.
Ramnaam bin Jeevana, koi na pahota paar._
(Taking refuge in Omkar, the whole world has gone astray; without Ram's Name, Jivan[dasji says], no one has ever reached the far shore.)

Jivandasji Maharaj says: by taking refuge in Omkar, all the people of the world have gone astray; without accepting the refuge of Ram's Name, no one has ever been saved from the ocean of worldly existence.

_Utpat pralay Oankaarme, moorakh na cheene maram.
Nyaare Harijan Jeevana, jahaa sadaa sanatan Brahm._
(Creation and dissolution occur within Omkar, but the fool does not understand this mystery; Hari's devotees, Jivan[dasji says], remain apart, dwelling always in the eternal Brahman.)

Jivandasji Maharaj says: the creation and dissolution of the universe take place within the essence of Omkar. Foolish people do not know this mystery, but Hari's devotees remain apart from this Omkar; they abide always in the eternal essence of Parabrahma.

_Ye ukaar akaar makaar, e teeno maaya joi.
Maaya hoi kar vistaraa, gyaani aape soi._
(These three — u, a, and ma — are the very form of Maya; Maya, taking these forms, has spread itself out, so the wise one himself has understood.)

Gyaniji Maharaj says: from these three sounds of Omkar — "u," "a," and "ma" — arises the essence of Maya present in this creation. Thus the essence of Omkar has spread forth, taking on the form of Maya — so Gyaniji has explained.

_Sat raj tam gun teenka, maaya dhari vistaar.
Gyaani maaya gun mayi, taaka anant vichaar._
(By bearing the three gunas — sattva, rajas, and tamas — Maya has spread herself out; Maya, made of the gunas, has endless purposes, the wise one reflects.)

Gyaniji Maharaj says: by taking on these three gunas — sattva, rajas, and tamas — Maya carries her own function through to completion. Thus this Maya, being made of the gunas, has countless purposes and intentions that never come to an end.

_Maaya upji Brahm te, Brahm rahyaa niradhaar.
Gyaani avarn Brahmaku, virlaa boojhan haar._
(Maya arose from Brahman, yet Brahman remains untouched by it; that indescribable Brahman is understood only by some rare soul.)

Gyaniji Maharaj says: Maya arises through Brahman, yet Brahman remains untouched and unattached by it. Such a Brahman cannot be described in words; only some rare soul can understand this mystery.

_Sat raj tam gun, teenka Sadguru kahya vichaar.
Oukaar ukaar akaar makaar, e gyaani gun niradhaar._
(Regarding the three gunas — sattva, rajas, and tamas — the Sadguru, reflecting, has declared: the u, a, and ma of Omkar are precisely these gunas themselves.)

Gyaniji Maharaj says: regarding these three gunas — sattva, rajas, and tamas — the Sadguru has said that the "u," "a," and "ma" of Omkar are precisely these gunas themselves.

_Kabir adhar dharanki shoonyme, soham shabdaapaar.
Jaake teke sab raha, yaa par hai niradhaar._
(Kabir says: in the void where there is no earth and no sky to rest upon, beyond even the word "Soham," is the one on whose support everything else rests — He alone is without support.)

Servant Kabirji says: even before the existence of the earth or the sky, and even before the word "Soham" itself, that on whose support all of this rests and endures is the divine…
